text:
[LNUL.4.2] **Boolean level — Kleene 3-valued logic.** `and` / `or` / `not`
operate over `{true, false, null}` by the standard Kleene tables:

| `a`     | `b`     | `a and b` | `a or b` |
|---------|---------|-----------|----------|
| `true`  | `null`  | `null`    | `true`   |
| `false` | `null`  | `false`   | `null`   |
| `null`  | `null`  | `null`    | `null`   |

and `not true = false`, `not false = true`, `not null = null`.

**A fault is absorbed, not propagated, by a deciding operand.** An operand
faults when evaluating it raises a trap ([LERR.1.4.1]), a `TypeError` or an
`EngineError` ([IRET.9.6]). `and` is `false` if any operand is `false`, wherever
it stands and whatever the others raise; it is a fault only if no operand is
`false`; and it is `null` only if none is `false` and none faults. `or` is the
dual: `true` if any operand is `true`. An implementation may evaluate the
operands in any order and may stop at a deciding operand.

An `EngineError` from anything but evaluating the operand — resource
exhaustion, a `pump_wcet_ns` overrun ([LERR.1.4.7]) — is not an operand's
fault. It halts the tier whatever the expression would answer.

**When several operands fault and none decides,** the expression yields one
fault, chosen by kind first — `EngineError`, then `TypeError`, then the trap
kinds in `proto/engine_error.proto#TrapKind` value order — and within a kind by
the fields of the record the fault is recorded as, in field-number order,
excluding `clock_ns` and `seq` ([RFCS.21.1]): at the first field that differs,
the lower value wins. A string field compares by its UTF-8 bytes as unsigned
values, a proper prefix before any longer string, and a field the record leaves
unset compares as its protobuf default, the empty string or `0`. The
offending operand's slot context ([LERR.9.12]) is among the fields compared.
Two faults that tie on every field record identically. An operand's position never enters, so `a and b` and
`b and a` agree on every input, faults included.

**Absorption and distributivity do not hold once faults exist:** `null and
(null or t)` is the fault `t`, not `null`. Commutativity, associativity, De
Morgan and double negation do.

alloy.name: lnul_4_2__best
alloy.note: T2I: the faults no other beats, by kind, then by recorded body. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

alloy.name: lnul_4_2__ok_where
alloy.note: A well-formed `where`: a trap or TypeError only from a conjunct that can raise by its declared types, null only from a nullable slot; an EngineError from any conjunct -- a value the artefact lied about.

alloy.name: lnul_4_2__out
alloy.note: What a conjunct yields: true, false, null, or a fault.

alloy.name: lnul_4_2__table
alloy.note: The absorbing `and` folded over the conjuncts: false, then a fault, then null, then true.

alloy.name: lnul_4_2__v5_refines_table
alloy.note: V5 REFINES THE TABLE: stopping at the first false in any order and absorbing every fault answers what the table answers. Letting a false not absorb an EngineError breaks it (TEETH).

idris.name: Lnul_4_2__answer
idris.note: The three Kleene values and a fourth, the trap: the clause's domain, which states what and and or do where an operand traps ([LERR.1.4.1]).

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and
idris.note: Kleene and on the three values; A TRAP IS ABSORBED ([LERR.1.4.1]): a false (for or, a true) on either side decides; otherwise a trap on either side is raised; otherwise Kleene's table.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and_commutes
idris.note: and commutes on every input, traps included: the clause's 'a and b and b and a agree on every input'.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__answer_of
idris.note: A result as a truth value: a non-Bool value is an ill-typed where, which the compiler refuses and [IRET.9.6] makes a fault, so it answers as a trap.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__not
idris.note: Swaps true and false, fixes null; a trap stays a trap.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__or
idris.note: Kleene or on the three values; A TRAP IS ABSORBED ([LERR.1.4.1]): a false (for or, a true) on either side decides; otherwise a trap on either side is raised; otherwise Kleene's table.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__or_commutes
idris.note: And so does or.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__result_of
idris.note: A truth value as a result again, so a connective's output is an operand.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__table
idris.note: The clause's table, row by row, and its three not cells, by Refl.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__trap_absorbed
idris.note: The cells absorption turns on, as table cells: trap and false, false and trap are false; trap and true traps; the or duals.

idris.name: Iret_7_5__test
idris.note: A join test answers a (token, candidate) pair true, false, null or a trap.

idris.name: iret_7_6__conj
idris.note: A node's tests combined: the absorbing `and` of their answers, true for none.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and_assoc
idris.note: The absorbing `and` is associative, traps included; with `lnul_4_2__and_commutes` a node's tests combine to one answer in any order.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and_left_comm
idris.note: Two conjuncts exchange across a third.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__null_not_false
idris.note: null is not false.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__trap_not_false
idris.note: A trap is not false.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__true_not_false
idris.note: true is not false.

idris.name: lnul_4_3__admits_and
idris.note: A positive node admits an `and` iff it admits both sides.

idris.name: lnul_4_7__blocks_and_decided
idris.note: A candidate whose first conjunct is decided blocks iff that conjunct holds and the rest blocks -- for any reading of a trap, since the decided conjunct is not one.

idris.name: iret_7_6__v5_is_conj_test
idris.note: A V5 `where` IS NetworkAnswer's combined test of its conjuncts, pointwise: the four-valued network and its view theorem (`iret_7_6__recompute_after_history_4`), which quantify over every test, take V5 wheres unchanged.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and5
idris.note: The V5 `and`. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and5_assoc
idris.note: The V5 `and` is associative, the yielded fault included. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and5_comm
idris.note: The V5 `and` is commutative, the yielded fault included; positional choice of the fault breaks it (TEETH T2). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and5_left_comm
idris.note: Two conjuncts exchange across a third.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and5_refines
idris.note: V5 REFINES THE TABLE: projected onto answers, `and5` is Rete/Eval.idr's absorbing `and`, cell for cell. V5 adds only which fault an `and` of two faults yields, on which the table is silent. Letting an EngineError escape a false breaks it (TEETH T1).

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and5_yes
idris.note: A true conjunct changes nothing.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__beats
idris.note: T2I: one fault beats another by kind, then by recorded body; position never enters. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__beats_asym
idris.note: Beating is asymmetric.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__beats_trans
idris.note: Beating is transitive.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__beats_tri
idris.note: Two faults neither of which beats the other are the same fault: T2I is a strict TOTAL order, which is what makes the recorded fault independent of order. Kind alone (T2K) is not total, and the order independence chain fails without the identity (TEETH T5).

idris.name: lnul_4_2__bestF
idris.note: The fault of two that V5 yields: the one that beats the other. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__bestF_assoc
idris.note: Which fault of three is yielded does not depend on grouping.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__bestF_comm
idris.note: Which fault is yielded does not depend on which side it stood.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__bestF_left
idris.note: A fault not beaten is yielded.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__bestF_right
idris.note: The beating fault is yielded.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__if_false
idris.note: The pick on false.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__if_true
idris.note: The pick on true.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__lexLt
idris.note: The lexicographic strict order on (priority, identity).

idris.name: lnul_4_2__lex_asym
idris.note: It is asymmetric.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__lex_trans
idris.note: It is transitive.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__lex_tri
idris.note: It is trichotomous.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__ltN
idris.note: The strict order on naturals, by structural recursion.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__ltN_asym
idris.note: It is asymmetric.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__ltN_trans
idris.note: It is transitive.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__ltN_tri
idris.note: It is trichotomous.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__not_beats
idris.note: If one fault does not beat another, the other beats it or they are one.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__or5
idris.note: The dual of `and5`: a true decides wherever it stands; otherwise T2I; otherwise null; otherwise false. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__or5_refines
idris.note: Projected onto answers, `or5` is Rete/Eval.idr's absorbing `or`, cell for cell.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__pick
idris.note: `if` by pattern, so the lemmas about it reduce.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__toAnswer
idris.note: An outcome as Rete/Eval.idr's answer: a fault of any kind is a trap there.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__v5
idris.note: A `where`'s answer under V5: its conjuncts combined by `and5`. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__v5_perm
idris.note: ORDER INDEPENDENCE: a `where`'s V5 answer does not depend on the order of its conjuncts -- [IRET.7.6]'s join tests 'may be evaluated in any order'. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_5_4__false_decides
idris.note: NARROWING: a false guard decides the `where` wherever it stands, whatever any other conjunct -- the guarded tail included -- would raise, and nothing is recorded: [IRET.9.6]'s narrowed tail evaluated before its guard meets a `false` guard that absorbs its TypeError. And folding a literal `false` operand is sound (RLOW.6.1.4). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: rfcs_21_1__selfjoin_v5_agrees
idris.note: Keyed on the recorded body, as T2I is, V5 records the same atom in either order. Fixing the identity breaks it (TEETH T5 against the self-join).

idris.name: rlow_6_1_4__absorption_fails
idris.note: ABSORPTION DOES NOT HOLD: `null and (null or t)` is the fault t, where the law would give null -- the clause's own example, so the compiler must not simplify by it.

idris.name: rlow_6_1_4__distributivity_fails
idris.note: DISTRIBUTIVITY DOES NOT HOLD: `null and (true or e)` is null, `(null and true) or (null and e)` is the EngineError e.
